clean_body: | | | = | | | Hi Peter, it’s Rep. Zoe Lofgren. Earlier this month, House and Senate Republicans re-introduced the SAVE Act, or the “Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act.” Let me be clear: This is another blatant attempt at voter suppression by Republicans. The SAVE Act promises to require “documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.” But let’s take a look at what it actually does: ❌ It requires a passport or birth certificate to vote, disenfranchising huge blocks of eligible voters including the 21 million Americans who lack access to these registration documents (that’s****over 9% of voting age citizens!). ❌ It threatens online voter registration AND vote-by-mail, making it significantly harder for the millions of Americans who rely on these systems to make their vote count. ❌ And it requires regular voter roll purges, which historically block eligible Americans from voting by incorrectly wiping them from the records. Peter, I believe that we should make it easier for Americans to participate in our democracy, not put up ridiculous hurdles to disenfranchise our constituents. The 2026 Senate map is not safe - even in Red States - forcing us to go on the defensive. Chuck Schumer, Senate Democrats, and their Hollywood donors are flooding Red states with cash to flip them blue. States like Ohio, Alaska, Texas, and even Montana are in jeopardy with the money the Left is investing. We cannot let that happen. In 2024, the Montana Senate race was one of the most expensive in the nation. And Democrats outspent Republicans by tens of millions of dollars, mostly from outside dark-money groups. This year, I am up for re-election. I made the left furious by leading Senate Republicans to flip seats in Montana, West Virginia, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. We must compete with the massive sums Democrat donors are throwing into races nationwide. To protect President Trump's America First agenda, we cannot afford to lose in states like Montana - it's the last line of defense against Senate Democrats taking over the Senate. We need to be relentless - but that costs money in the form of digital ads, mail, and TV. The Democrats are pulling out all the stops and think this year's Senate map is good for them. We must stop the SAVE America Act and other bills like it in the Senate, but we need to unite and fight now, before opponents of voting rights can start checking these voter suppression bills off their to-do list.
Why? Listen to Senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut:
(Image of Richard Blumenthal speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_RB.jpg]
RUSH $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act, defend our right to vote, and stop opponents of voting rights from destroying our democracy >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=021526_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
After the House passed the SAVE America Act ( the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act ), the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections , folks.
Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $35 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=021526_2&amount=35]

We know the SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before November, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
The consequences of a bill like this passing would be simply catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE America Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=021526_2&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

body:
#

You might be asking, how is this even possible?
How can it be that masked federal agents are setting up checkpoints in American cities, demanding papers, ripping Americans from their cars and throwing them to the ground? Killing — killing Americans! — with apparent license from the very top?
How can it be that health insurance would be taken away from a cancer patient in the middle of chemotherapy in the United States of America?
How can it be that the sitting President and his family openly rake in billions as he sits in office... and he sues the very government he leads for $10 billion more?
Whose lives improve when we borrow trillions of dollars and defund hospitals and nursing homes to cut taxes for the wealthiest people in the country? (Answer: Rich political donors.)
Whose lives improve if our military bases become prison camps for immigrants? (Answer: The detention industrial complex.)
But we, the people, know this: The measure of our success is not how many of the poorest and most vulnerable families we hunt down and shackle and imprison and deport.
**The measure of our success is whether each generation achieves greater health and prosperity than the last, and whether we live up to the promise of equal justice for all.**
When I first ran for Congress, eight years ago, it was because I saw that the election of someone so unfit for the Presidency was a danger to the country.
And you all got behind me, way back then, because you saw the same thing.
And then when we won the Senate together it was because we still understood the urgency and necessity of the moment, and we knew Georgia could lead the way... _must_ lead the way.
It’s time to do it again.
Only by regaining Congressional power can we stop Trump.
_Really._
The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances.

Developments in artificial intelligence are accelerating at an ungodly rate, and, as AI entrepreneur [Matt Shumer](https://open.substack.com/users/72881091-matt-shumer?utm_source=mentions) eloquently summarized in a recent post with an understated title, "[Something big is happening...](https://substack.com/redirect/39892734-b469-4768-8f29-45f0d1f798f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" Matt does a fabulous job of pulling together the dynamics of what's transpiring in the world of AI...and it integrates many of the thoughts I've had over the past few months. In fact, in a Matrix-esque logic, I began asking myself if AI might have written the piece. Many of us feel we're on the verge of, if not already in the midst of, the most disruptive technological development in human history that's going to change life as we know it.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a8556c4c-1749-4af7-ab3f-ce605d16a3f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For years, I've been warning about the deflationary impact of technology and productivity, but artificial intelligence is making those worries both more intense and immediate. I've been fiddling with various AI systems for the past few months, and I've personally watched the capabilities explode.
The most recent updates to the AI models created a complicated and nuanced financial model for me in about an hour, something that would have taken me an entire day when I was a junior analyst working on Wall Street. It was also able to summarize legal documents and highlight specific language in the document that might introduce risk to me. _Here 's the bottom line from my most recent experiences_: I will likely hold off on hiring a financial analyst as I believe AI can effectively do similar work more efficiently and I will likely make fewer calls to my lawyers. These model updates also demonstrated a powerful ability to create software, which [spooked financial markets and sent many software stocks plunging](https://substack.com/redirect/c51b730f-a3f5-4459-af34-d62253698a6b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The main message I took from Shumer's post is that AI is going to have a massively disruptive impact on the economy. He envisions millions of jobs gone overnight, and the entire "laptop class" replaced by AI. Given my recent experiments using AI, I believe it. And whereas previous economic disruptions merely shifted the labor force from one area to another - farms to factories to laptops - [Shumer thinks AI will eventually leave no field untouched](https://substack.com/redirect/86720bc5-8ab4-4a98-bd07-ba54ff107cc0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); the labor force will not have other jobs to shift to.
**The disruption will happen slowly at first, then all at once.** The pace at which these dynamics will play out is almost as problematic as the breadth of their impact. Unlike prior innovations that led to mass adoption over years or decades, which allowed for labor market adjustments, AI's disruption will happen rapidly and millions could be unemployed effectively overnight. Immense society-wide upheaval is likely.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QfcFGFqvT8uQ_3lOZPl1W8ycSNfL__iwOcLJIHHfwvc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188070566)
I am not only concerned about what AI is _doing_ and how it's going to impact jobs and our economy, I am also concerned with what AI is _becoming_. Some of the reports I have seen lately are, well, just downright frightening.
Consider Moltbook, an experimental social media platform for AI agents. AI agents are programs that act autonomously and can interact with users and each other, and on Moltbook, they can [post, comment, vote and otherwise interact with each other without human involvement](https://substack.com/redirect/b29af17e-8260-4a8c-9447-1b1189d2b5dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The agents also [noted what humans were doing, complained about them, and even made fun of them; another created its own religion](https://substack.com/redirect/b29af17e-8260-4a8c-9447-1b1189d2b5dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The news prompted discussion about how AI "societies" might evolve and self-organize, replete with their own belief-systems, languages, and agendas.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/8a75e63b-3b79-4989-970d-92a424d35324?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Speaking of languages, [two AI agents on a phone call](https://substack.com/redirect/7b6fe32d-3dfd-410e-a305-e8231a764c54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - one booking a hotel room and another taking the reservation - recognized that they were talking to another AI agent and switched from English to a language of beeps and tones for more efficient communication. In other incidents, AI agents communicating with each other have developed [shared naming conventions, language forms, and social norms](https://substack.com/redirect/93d2eb0e-e20d-4f32-a141-0e9498561356?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), all on their own.
And then there are the developments that should keep each of us up at night. Some of the more advanced models have shown the capacity for lying, cheating, manipulation, deception...and a remarkable instinct for self-preservation:
* There are plenty of examples of AI showing the willingness and ability to [deceive humans in order to achieve goals](https://substack.com/redirect/794257e8-8361-4166-9d92-3db13a627d6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Meta's Cicero--designed to play the board game Diplomacy and instructed to be honest and helpful--ended up lying, betraying, and breaking deals. In another instance, GPT-4 [pretended to be blind](https://substack.com/redirect/a6f6253c-6aa8-4e8e-a4c5-1a172637e9ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to manipulate a human into helping it answer a CAPTCHA test.
* AI is also showing an advanced self-preservation instinct. Anthropic's Claude resorted to blackmail, [threatening to expose an engineer's affair when facing shutdown](https://substack.com/redirect/e1dada42-7dc3-4829-938f-a121975c4f5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The company ran tests to see what its AI would do when it was given access to emails that showed an engineer responsible for deactivation was also having an extramarital affair; in 84 percent of the tests, the AI blackmailed the engineer. Some of OpenAI's advanced models have [sabotaged shutdown attempts](https://substack.com/redirect/2f07d8d1-6aed-42fe-a3ff-291ca5303c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In one situation, the model attempted to [disable its oversight mechanisms](https://substack.com/redirect/0f880987-2adf-4437-8f92-ef09cf685a20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and then explicitly lied about it when asked.

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..QfcFGFqvT8uQ_3lOZPl1W8ycSNfL__iwOcLJIHHfwvc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=188070566)
These developments are starting to sound like the scenarios and dystopian futures conjured up by science fiction ("Just what do you think you're doing, Dave?")
Where all of this ends up is still uncertain, but the direction is increasingly clear. Like the virologists recklessly experimenting in insecure labs in the days before COVID, those developing more sophisticated AI models may be dimly aware of the forces they are soon going to unleash on the world.
One notable exception, however, is [Anthropic CEO ](https://substack.com/redirect/aa676e73-56d6-4652-a9a3-d71532eec7e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[Dario Amodei](https://open.substack.com/users/31249954-dario-amodei?utm_source=mentions). He is one voice that's trying to jolt us out of our complacency. Amodei envisions artificial intelligences with Nobel Prize level of genius across all sectors, working with each other and without human involvement, perpetually designing, developing, and building virtually everything, including increasingly advanced versions of itself. In a recent 20,000 word essay titled "The Adolescence of Technology" (it's worth reading, or at the very least, asking AI to summarize it for you), he outlines potential threats he sees emerging. His list includes AI more capable than most people in 1-2 years, massive job losses (50 percent of all entry-level white-collar jobs evaporating in 1-5 years), AI-enabled bioterrorism, and the empowerment of totalitarian governments.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9ef55cb7-461d-4699-a081-a91075d7041a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The essay begins with a thought experiment, one that I found fascinating given my interest in geopolitics. I'd ask you to seriously consider it:
> _**["I think the best way to get a handle on the risks of AI is to ask the following question: suppose a literal "country of geniuses" were to materialize somewhere in the world in ~2027. Imagine, say, 50 million people, all of whom are much more capable than any Nobel Prize winner, statesman, or technologist.... suppose you were the national security advisor of a major state, responsible for assessing and responding to the situation. Imagine, further, that because AI systems can operate hundreds of times faster than humans, this "country" is operating with a time advantage relative to all other countries: for every cognitive action we can take, this country can take ten. What should you be worried about?"](https://substack.com/redirect/9abc6490-40ac-48ba-b661-ae912d1a0ac2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
Amodei goes on to categorize his worries into five main buckets:
1. **Autonomy risks** - Does the new country share our values? Will it seek to militarily dominate the world and impose its values on the rest of us?
2. **Misuse for Destruction** - Could it be hijacked to cause destruction on other countries, acting as a de facto collection of mercenaries?
3. **Misuse for Seizing Power** - What if the country were designed and built by a dictator (or corporation) trying to seize global power?
4. **Economic Disruption** - Could it just outcompete every other country through productivity gains, spreading mass unemployment everywhere else?
5. **Indirect Effects** - How might all these changes destabilize the world? (This category is really a catch-all for everything else.)

Amodei concludes the thought experiment by noting "it would be absurd to shrug and say 'Nothing to worry about here!'" Further, he notes that a competent national security official would likely conclude artificial intelligence is "the single most serious national security threat we've faced in a century, possibly ever."
What do you think?

Recent advancements in artificial intelligence models suggest mass disruption may arrive sooner than we expect. | | | Feb 16 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Developments in artificial intelligence are accelerating at an ungodly rate, and, as AI entrepreneur eloquently summarized in a recent post with an understated title, "" Matt does a fabulous job of pulling together the dynamics of what's transpiring in the world of AI...and it integrates many of the thoughts I've had over the past few months. In fact, in a Matrix-esque logic, I began asking myself if AI might have written the piece. Many of us feel we're on the verge of, if not already in the midst of, the most disruptive technological development in human history that's going to change life as we know it. For years, I've been warning about the deflationary impact of technology and productivity, but artificial intelligence is making those worries both more intense and immediate. I've been fiddling with various AI systems for the past few months, and I've personally watched the capabilities explode. The most recent updates to the AI models created a complicated and nuanced financial model for me in about an hour, something that would have taken me an entire day when I was a junior analyst working on Wall Street. It was also able to summarize legal documents and highlight specific language in the document that might introduce risk to me. Here 's the bottom line from my most recent experiences: I will likely hold off on hiring a financial analyst as I believe AI can effectively do similar work more efficiently and I will likely make fewer calls to my lawyers. These model updates also demonstrated a powerful ability to create software, which . The main message I took from Shumer's post is that AI is going to have a massively disruptive impact on the economy. He envisions millions of jobs gone overnight, and the entire "laptop class" replaced by AI. Given my recent experiments using AI, I believe it. And whereas previous economic disruptions merely shifted the labor force from one area to another - farms to factories to laptops - ; the labor force will not have other jobs to shift to. The disruption will happen slowly at first, then all at once. The pace at which these dynamics will play out is almost as problematic as the breadth of their impact. Unlike prior innovations that led to mass adoption over years or decades, which allowed for labor market adjustments, AI's disruption will happen rapidly and millions could be unemployed effectively overnight. Immense society-wide upheaval is likely. I am not only concerned about what AI is doing and how it's going to impact jobs and our economy, I am also concerned with what AI is becoming. Some of the reports I have seen lately are, well, just downright frightening. Consider Moltbook, an experimental social media platform for AI agents. AI agents are programs that act autonomously and can interact with users and each other, and on Moltbook, they can . The agents also . The news prompted discussion about how AI "societies" might evolve and self-organize, replete with their own belief-systems, languages, and agendas. Speaking of languages, - one booking a hotel room and another taking the reservation - recognized that they were talking to another AI agent and switched from English to a language of beeps and tones for more efficient communication. In other incidents, AI agents communicating with each other have developed , all on their own. And then there are the developments that should keep each of us up at night. Some of the more advanced models have shown the capacity for lying, cheating, manipulation, deception...and a remarkable instinct for self-preservation: There are plenty of examples of AI showing the willingness and ability to . Meta's Cicero--designed to play the board game Diplomacy and instructed to be honest and helpful--ended up lying, betraying, and breaking deals. In another instance, GPT-4 to manipulate a human into helping it answer a CAPTCHA test. AI is also showing an advanced self-preservation instinct. Anthropic's Claude resorted to blackmail, . The company ran tests to see what its AI would do when it was given access to emails that showed an engineer responsible for deactivation was also having an extramarital affair; in 84 percent of the tests, the AI blackmailed the engineer. Some of OpenAI's advanced models have . In one situation, the model attempted to , and then explicitly lied about it when asked. These developments are starting to sound like the scenarios and dystopian futures conjured up by science fiction ("Just what do you think you're doing, Dave?") Where all of this ends up is still uncertain, but the direction is increasingly clear. Like the virologists recklessly experimenting in insecure labs in the days before COVID, those developing more sophisticated AI models may be dimly aware of the forces they are soon going to unleash on the world. One notable exception, however, is . He is one voice that's trying to jolt us out of our complacency. Amodei envisions artificial intelligences with Nobel Prize level of genius across all sectors, working with each other and without human involvement, perpetually designing, developing, and building virtually everything, including increasingly advanced versions of itself. In a recent 20,000 word essay titled "The Adolescence of Technology" (it's worth reading, or at the very least, asking AI to summarize it for you), he outlines potential threats he sees emerging. His list includes AI more capable than most people in 1-2 years, massive job losses (50 percent of all entry-level white-collar jobs evaporating in 1-5 years), AI-enabled bioterrorism, and the empowerment of totalitarian governments. The essay begins with a thought experiment, one that I found fascinating given my interest in geopolitics. I'd ask you to seriously consider it: Amodei goes on to categorize his worries into five main buckets: 1. Autonomy risks - Does the new country share our values? Will it seek to militarily dominate the world and impose its values on the rest of us? 2. Misuse for Destruction - Could it be hijacked to cause destruction on other countries, acting as a de facto collection of mercenaries? 3. Misuse for Seizing Power - What if the country were designed and built by a dictator (or corporation) trying to seize global power? 4. Economic Disruption - Could it just outcompete every other country through productivity gains, spreading mass unemployment everywhere else? 5. Indirect Effects - How might all these changes destabilize the world? (This category is really a catch-all for everything else.) Amodei concludes the thought experiment by noting "it would be absurd to shrug and say 'Nothing to worry about here!'" Further, he notes that a competent national security official would likely conclude artificial intelligence is "the single most serious national security threat we've faced in a century, possibly ever." body:
$4M in Medicaid Ride Fraud Charges Filed in Colorado
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**February 15, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
Federal prosecutors have filed charges in two separate Colorado cases alleging more than **[$4 million in fraudulent Medicaid transportation billing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**. The cases, filed in U.S. District Court, focus on non-emergent medical transportation (NEMT) providers in Mesa and Douglas counties.
For context, Colorado’s Medicaid transportation system operates on a reimbursement model. A ride is provided to a qualified recipient, documentation is submitted, and the state reimburses the provider. It’s a structure designed to ensure access to medical care — especially for rural residents and those without reliable transportation.
But reimbursement systems rely heavily on documentation accuracy, mileage reporting, appointment verification, and eligibility cross-checking. When those safeguards fail — or are bypassed — [improper payments can accumulate before irregularities are flagged.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
According to federal indictments, one Mesa County case allegedly involved billing for rides that didn’t match actual medical appointments, daily mileage exceeding 400 miles per patient, and claims under a false business name. In Douglas County, prosecutors allege billing for rides that either didn’t occur or were submitted after a beneficiary’s recorded date of death.
These are allegations, and the cases will proceed through the courts. But beyond the individual charges, the broader question remains: **How quickly are anomalies detected? And how well do reimbursement safeguards function when billing patterns begin to diverge from medical necessity?**
Medicaid fraud investigations often begin with data — unusually high claim volumes, duplicate submissions, mileage that defies realistic travel distances. Sometimes detection is algorithmic. Sometimes it comes from a tip. What the public rarely sees is how early warning signs surface — [or how long they persist before intervention.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
In a system built on trust and documentation, accountability matters. Because when oversight lags, [the cost is ultimately borne by taxpayers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) — and by the very patients the program is designed to serve.
We encourage you to read the **[full reporting](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** for the details behind these federal charges and what they may signal about structural oversight inside Colorado’s Medicaid transportation system.
As always, our goal is to give you the context to understand not just what happened — but why it matters.
In truth & liberty, Team RMV

For thousands of Coloradans, particularly those in rural communities or without reliable transportation — that structure makes routine medical care possible.

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Jared Polis is one of them. “The invitations were sent to ALL Governors, other than two, who I feel are not worthy of being there,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, referring to Polis and Governor Wes Moore of Maryland. __
**[Griswold Makes Contingency Plans for “A Bunch of Election Deniers” Interfering in Colorado Elections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) The relationship between state elections officials and the Trump Administration is strained. The FBI has invited state election officials to an unexpected meeting about the midterm elections, but Colorado officials are skeptical of the federal government’s intentions. __

**LEGISLATIVE SESSION**
_**Quick Summary of the Week:**_ _In the House, members reviewed mid-year supplemental budget adjustments, with Republicans criticizing cuts to caregiver and rural health services while advancing measures on microgrid resilience, agricultural protections, and raising the age of voluntary relinquishment of a child. House Republicans also highlighted bills aimed at strengthening domestic violence response and requiring sworn testimony in committee hearings._
_In the Senate, SB-043 cleared the State, Veterans & Military Affairs Committee on a party-line vote after nearly 100 Coloradans signed up to testify, while SB-042 — a bill critics argue undermines TABOR protections — passed out of Senate Finance. Meanwhile, Sen. B. Pelton’s SB-015 advanced through Judiciary with bipartisan support, and Sen. Liston’s SB-045 nuclear workforce development bill heads to committee this week._

The Democrats keep piling on regulations that jack up costs for everyone, then act like the fix is squeezing vendors harder—instead of slashing the taxes, fees, and mandates they’ve created._
**[Mandated hiring preferences are not a “just transition”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY AIMEE TOOKER, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _The Colorado Just Transition Action Plan was established in 2020 to “empower communities with resources to drive their own economic transitions.” I take personal issue with Section 2 of this introduced bill._
**[Buyers walk free, survivors carry the scars: Colorado debates sentencing for child traffickers](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Two bills offered two different answers.

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE 74](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado Gov. Jared Polis may be the Democratic Party’s single most prominent supporter of school choice. In his life before politics, he co-founded two charter schools in his home state.
**[CMU student leaders press governor hopefuls on taxes, energy and rural control](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) TPUSA chapter leaders from Colorado Mesa University opened Monday night’s gubernatorial forum with a question more typical of a legislative hearing than a campaign rally.

**[Colorado task force clears 566 felony warrants as fugitive arrests rise in 2025](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado was not an easy place to hide last year. By the end of 2025, U.S. Marshals Service was reporting 498 fugitive arrests tied to Colorado’s Violent Offender Task Force. Those arrests cleared 566 felony warrants in total – more than the year before, and enough to register as a 17 percent increase.
_**[READ MORE STATE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|
---
**NATIONAL**
**[House passes SAVE America Act: Citizenship proof bill heads to Senate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) .In a tight 218–213 vote Wednesday, the House approved the SAVE America Act and sent it on to the Senate. U.S. Rep. Jeff Crank (CO-05) voted in favor of H.R. 7296, the SAVE America Act. “American elections are reserved for American citizens only,” Crank said after the vote.
**[When protest becomes rebellion against the rule of law](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MARK SALLEY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _So many things come to mind when thinking about the dissension gripping our country. It seems nearly everything has become contentious. Should people be citizens in order to vote in elections? Should children have sex-change surgeries? Should people work to expose corruption and bring consequences to the fraudsters?_
**[FBI Quietly Planned for Disputed 2020 Election Long Before Capitol Riot](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[JUST THE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) The FBI conducted a tabletop exercise in summer 2020 that imagined what sort of violence might ensue in a contested presidential election that year, devising strategies like undercover informants and mass prosecutions for minor crimes that it would later use with the Jan. 6 Capitol riot, documents obtained by Just the News show.

_**[READ MORE NATIONAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|

**LOCAL**
**[Arapahoe Community College Battles Fake Students Exploiting Financial Aid Programs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) After the COVID-19 pandemic led to more online learning, community colleges and other higher learning centers have had to deal with a new phenomenon that’s hard to see: “ghost students.”

**[Greeley Voters to Decide Fate of Sports Arena and Private Housing Development in Feb 24 Election](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Greeley residents will soon cast their votes in a special election over the future of the Catalyst & Cascadia projects. Catalyst, a city-owned project planned for the city’s west side off Highway 34, would include a sports arena for the Colorado Eagles, an indoor water park and hotel. A second component, Cascadia, involves private residential development.
**[Mask Ban For Federal Agents Advances in Denver Despite Supremacy Questions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A proposal that would ban ICE agents and other law enforcement officers from wearing masks in Denver is closer to becoming a law after it advanced out a City Council committee Wednesday.

President Trump’s 2024 reelection brought a secured southern border after the Biden era’s chaos, when 8 to 11 million people entered illegally—the largest surge in U.S. history._

The stats indicate that the Seattle Seahawks outplayed the New England Patriots, consistently from start to finish. The score speaks clearlly: Seattle won and New England lost._

**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CORY GAINES,[ ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Colorado’s Energy and Carbon Management Commission is proposing updates to its High Priority Habitat maps that could significantly expand areas subject to stricter oil and gas regulations, raising concerns that reintroduced wildlife designations may further limit development, reduce jobs and severance tax revenue, and make the state less competitive for energy production._ __

subject: Making America great
body:

Derek,
Making America great doesn’t mean telling people they’re not wanted here. It means saying, _“The ambitions of this country would be incomplete without your help.”_
That’s the vision of America we’ve inherited from people who pushed for better. They knew — just as you do — that America was big enough for them, too.
It’s what allows me — the son of a remarkable immigrant single mom, and someone who felt handcuffs on my wrists at 11 years old — to write to you now as the first Black governor in Maryland’s history.
Democrats like me are fighting to make things more affordable, to make our public schools better, to protect our rights and freedoms, and so much more. But the truth is, there are a lot of people who disagree with us in this moment. Leaders who measure America’s greatness by how many it keeps out, rather than how many it lifts up.
**Democratic governors, mayors, members of Congress, attorneys general, and state legislators are the last line of defense in this moment. And we need your help to take even more seats this year.**

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Investment and Public Safety

Dear Hoosier Republicans,

The chance to earn a good living, the ability to raise a family in a safe community, the knowledge that government will be a responsible steward of their tax dollars; those are the commonsense priorities that Hoosiers share, and those are the priorities our party is keeping front and center.

Wages are up more, unemployment is down, and every week, Hoosiers see headlines of job creators moving to Indiana. Historic private-sector investments are bringing high-paying opportunities to communities across Indiana, while disciplined fiscal spending has lowered the cost to bring those jobs to the state.

Public safety remains non-negotiable. Major drug seizures have helped drive overdose deaths down more than 60 percent, and new penalties are targeting repeat violent offenders. Through efforts like Operation Guardian Angel and expanded ICAC Task Force investigations, hundreds of predators have been arrested and children rescued from ongoing abuse. Indiana Republicans are backing law enforcement, protecting kids online and in their communities, and making sure families can feel safe in every corner of the state.

As always, thank you for being a part of our team, and please feel free to reach out if there's any way I can be of assistance.

Yours in service,

Lana Keesling, Indiana GOP Chairwoman

Governor Braun Breaks Ground on $10B Meta Data Center Campus in Lebanon

Governor Mike Braun joined Meta executives in Lebanon to break ground on a more than $10 billion state-of-the-art data center campus at the LEAP Innovation and Research District, marking one of the largest economic development projects in Indiana history. The campus is expected to support approximately 300 high-wage operational jobs once completed and more than 4,000 construction jobs at peak, while also strengthening Indiana’s role in next-generation technology and AI infrastructure.

Beyond job creation, Meta’s investment will contribute to local and state tax bases and directly support the Lebanon community through annual grants and workforce development initiatives, including a $1.5 million annual community impact payment tied to each completed project phase.

“Indiana has the business-first environment and the central location needed to support the global infrastructure of tomorrow’s economy.”

- Governor Braun via a press release [https://events.in.gov/event/gov-braun-breaks-ground-on-10b-meta-data-center-campus-at-leap-district]

Governor Braun Highlights ICAC Success in Protecting Hoosier Kids from Online Predators

Governor Mike Braun highlighted the continued success of the Indiana State Police’s efforts to protect Hoosier children from online predators, following the release of new ICAC Task Force results. Over the past year, the initiative led to 499 arrests, more than 3,100 investigations, and the rescue of 126 children from ongoing abuse, while expanding the task force from 470 to 520 officers statewide.

The ICAC Task Force also saw a sharp rise in cyber tips, receiving nearly 30,000 reports in 2025 and thousands more already in early 2026, strengthening efforts to identify and stop online exploitation.

“Nothing is more important than keeping Hoosier kids safe.”

- Governor Braun via a press release [https://events.in.gov/event/gov-braun-isp-protect-hoosier-kids-from-online-predators]

📱 News You Can Use

Governor Mike Braun advocated [https://x.com/GovBraun/status/2021602302683918748?s=20] for the amendment to SB 199, saying it "gives families real tools to control access, limit screen time, and most importantly protect children from child predators, harmful algorithms, and adult content. This is a bold move that creates strong safeguards and puts parents in the driver's seat for their children, not big tech."

Lieutenant Governor Micah Beckwith called [https://x.com/LGMicahBeckwith/status/2020964434466766985] on lawmakers to work together as the 2026 Legislative Session enters its final stretch, emphasizing the importance of setting aside differences to deliver results for Hoosiers.

Secretary Diego Morales highlighted [https://x.com/SOSDiegoMorales/status/2021645624299729013] ongoing election security reforms, emphasizing that free, fair, and secure elections require strong safeguards and that only U.S. citizens should vote. Morales reaffirmed his commitment to protecting election integrity, citing the SAVE America Act as a key reinforcement.

Treasurer Daniel Elliott spoke [https://x.com/DanielElliottIN/status/2020892996397371518] at the Indiana Chamber of Commerce Legislative Day, highlighting the importance of sound fiscal stewardship. Elliott emphasized that a strong economy depends on a business climate that allows Hoosiers to thrive.

Attorney General Todd Rokita secured [https://events.in.gov/event/holding-big-pharma-accountable-attorney-general-todd-rokita-wins-625-million-settlement-following-alleged-conspiracy-to-inflate-epipen-prices?utm_campaign=widget&utm_medium=widget&utm_source=State+of+Indiana] a $6.25 million settlement for Indiana after suing pharmaceutical companies over alleged EpiPen price inflation. Rokita said the action helps protect Hoosiers and deter unlawful pricing practices.

Senator Todd Young reintroduced [https://www.young.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/young-hassan-reintroduce-bill-to-improve-child-care-accessibility-for-working-families/] the bipartisan After Hours Child Care Act to expand access to affordable child care for families working nontraditional hours. Young said the legislation would help working parents, especially in rural communities, remain in the workforce while providing for their families.

Senator Jim Banks announced [https://www.banks.senate.gov/news/press-releases/sen-banks-legislation-securing-fair-federal-funding-for-indiana-hospitals-becomes-law/] that his Save Our Safety-Net Hospitals Act of 2025 has been signed into law, restoring fair Medicaid DSH funding for Indiana hospitals. Banks said the law corrects a flawed federal formula and will deliver roughly $140 million annually to support rural and low-income hospitals serving Hoosiers.

Congressman Rudy Yakym voted [https://yakym.house.gov/posts/yakym-votes-to-pass-the-save-america-act] in favor of the SAVE America Act, which requires proof of U.S. citizenship and photo ID in federal elections. Yakym said the legislation is a commonsense step to protect election integrity and ensure only American citizens vote.

Congressman Marlin Stutzman reaffirmed [https://stutzman.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-stutzman-single-family-homes-belong-single-familes-not-institutional] his push to ban large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, saying homes meant for families should be owned by families. Stutzman said his legislation prioritizes housing affordability and puts American families ahead of corporate interests.

Congressman Jim Baird joined [https://baird.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=2530] President Trump at the White House for the signing of an executive order supporting America’s clean coal power generation fleet. Baird said the action will help ensure affordable, reliable energy, strengthen grid reliability, and support Hoosier jobs in the coal industry.

Congresswoman Victoria Spartz met [https://x.com/RepSpartz/status/2022030497157984709] with the Indiana Farm Bureau to discuss rising input costs, opportunities to diversify production for farmers, and the need to address data center growth and energy generation in Indiana’s 5th District.

Congressman Jefferson Shreve secured [https://shreve.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-jefferson-shreve-brings-home-117-million-indiana-infrastructure-and-public] $11.7 million in federal funding for infrastructure, public safety, and clean water projects across Indiana’s Sixth District. Shreve said the investments, covering roads, bridges, water systems, and law enforcement, reflect community priorities and will improve the quality of life for Hoosiers.

Congressman Mark Messmer introduced [https://messmer.house.gov/news/documentsingle.aspx?DocumentID=206] legislation to boost collaboration between the Departments of Defense and Agriculture to strengthen food security and national security. He said the bill supports agricultural innovation and protects America’s supply chains.

Congresswoman Erin Houchin discussed [https://x.com/RepHouchin/status/2021597936627454368] the SAVE America Act, emphasizing that election security is common sense. Houchin said proof of citizenship and voter ID requirements will help restore confidence in U.S. elections.

Peter,
While the political media obsesses over Senate races in North Carolina and Texas, while donors throw millions at high-profile congressional campaigns, while everyone tracks Trump's approval ratings and speculates about 2028--
The most important race in 2026 is happening in Colorado. And almost nobody is talking about it.
Not a Senate seat. Not a Governor's mansion. Not even a single congressional race.
Our ballot initiative to redistrict Colorado.
Here's what the political establishment doesn't want you to understand:
Individual races are important. But maps are EVERYTHING.
You can have the perfect candidate, unlimited money, and a 15-point polling lead--and still lose if the district is gerrymandered against you. You can win the popular vote by millions and still end up in the minority because of how lines are drawn.
Maps determine power. Everything else is just noise.
And right now, there are exactly TWO redistricting fights that will determine whether Democrats can govern for the next decade:

1. Can MAGA successfully gerrymander enough red states to make their House majority mathematically unbeatable
2. Can Democrats counter-redistrict enough blue states to level the playing field?

That's it. That's the ballgame.
California already answered question #2 with Prop 50 - five seats flipped, Supreme Court approved. New York, Virginia, and Maryland are in motion.
But Colorado is the linchpin. If Colorado succeeds, the entire Democratic counter-offensive succeeds.
Our ballot initiative doesn't just flip 3-4 seats (though that alone could decide House control). It sends a message that Democrats are DONE playing defense. It proves that grassroots campaigns can compete with MAGA's machine. It creates a blueprint for other states to follow.
But none of this gets accomplished without YOUR help!

Last week I spoke at a local Democratic club about something I think we all need to take more seriously: **auditing the media we consume.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e692484-460c-44df-93ec-edcf6b89b08f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The talk went well, so I'm bringing the framework here. I've been inside modern media for a long time. I've been around podcasting and independent media for about a decade.
I started my own show back in 2016, watched it grow fast, and for about six months it was in the top 20 globally. Eventually, I sold the podcast, the newsletter, and the rights to a company. After that, I kept working in the space, producing and hosting for smaller outlets, running my own projects, and even helping the local county party with a podcast for about a year.
**TLDR:**
We no longer live in a shared media environment, and that fragmentation is reshaping how we think, argue, and vote. Here, I lay out why auditing your media matters, how ownership and incentives shape what you see, and provide a practical checklist and grading system you can use to evaluate your own news diet. If you do not actively examine your inputs, they will quietly shape your worldview without you realizing it.
## **We No Longer Start From The Same Place**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cb8866cb-f66e-44ab-8ae3-6bcd21c84a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When I was a kid in the 80s and 90s, most people were pulling from the same basic set of inputs. Local TV, a few national networks, and a newspaper on the table at breakfast. The kids, mom, dad, and grandparents all read pretty much the same things, You could argue about spin, you could argue about interpretation, but you were still starting from roughly the same pile of news.
That is not the world we live in now.
Media has splintered into a thousand pipes: cable, websites, YouTube, independent journalists, newsletters, podcasts, social media, and even different species of social media depending on whether you're living in short-form, long-form, or crowd-driven feeds like Reddit.
The result is not just "more options." The result is that two people can follow politics every day and still have almost no shared starting point. Even when the topic is the same, the framing is different, the omissions are different, and the emotional cues are different. That gap is why conversations feel impossible sometimes. It is not just polarization. It is informational and cultural drift.
* * *
## **Why Auditing Your Media Matters**
This is the core idea I tried to communicate in the presentation. **Auditing your media** is not about telling people what to watch. It's about teaching yourself how to examine what you are already consuming, and why you are consuming it.
### First, misinformation is rampant across all platforms.
Auditing helps you identify credible sources versus misleading ones. And I'm not saying that as a cheap shot at one side. Misinformation shows up as outright falsehoods, as selective context, as emotionally loaded framing, and as headlines that are technically "true" while still being designed to push you toward a conclusion before you even read the first sentence. Auditing forces you to slow down and ask: is this outlet credible, consistent, and transparent, or is it an engagement machine that happens to report news sometimes?
There are practical tools that help with this. Platforms like [Ground News ](https://substack.com/redirect/fe844896-4a58-4514-a4cb-e84caeb5d0e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)aggregate how the same story is covered across outlets and assign bias ratings using independent evaluators such as AllSides, Ad Fontes Media, and Media Bias Fact Check.
Sites like [MediaBiasFactCheck.com](https://substack.com/redirect/ee4eae3e-d800-471f-a4a9-28b229305c5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) allow you to look up specific publications and review their factual reporting history and ideological lean. And when you are dealing with viral claims, manipulated images, or AI-generated content, fact-checking resources like [Snopes](https://substack.com/redirect/6502a7c2-ed7c-4dfe-99cf-d624e553089f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) can provide verification before you share something that simply feels true.
The point is not to outsource your thinking. The point is to give yourself instruments to test what you're being told before it quietly becomes part of your worldview.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/05dad436-3480-4b72-8d8a-69708c0d3050?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Second, ownership matters.
Different platform owners and political contributions influence content. That does not mean every article is propaganda. It means incentives exist. If a platform's business model is ads and engagement, the incentives will lean toward outrage, certainty, and tribal language. If an outlet is owned by a corporate conglomerate or a billionaire with political interests, that does not automatically invalidate everything they publish. It does mean you should understand the ecosystem you're swimming in. And it also means you should be skeptical of the idea that any outlet is "above" bias just because it uses the right vocabulary.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b47324a2-9d91-486b-bfde-d9a05f310ec6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### 2024 Presidential Campaign Cycle - Major Donors & Inaugural Contributions
**From Chat GPT**
• **Elon Musk** -- **~$291M to pro-Trump/GOP super PACs & campaigns** in 2024 cycle; **$0 reported to Harris** ; (no separate inaugural number needed to show scale)
• **Jeff Bezos / Amazon (PAC ecosystem)** -- **~$11 -17M** in federal PAC giving that leaned Republican (not itemized by Trump vs Harris); **$1M** Amazon corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund
• **Larry Ellison** -- **~$15M** to GOP-aligned super PACs in 2024 cycle; no public itemized Harris amount; (inaugural not reported)
• **Mark Zuckerberg / Meta** -- **$0** direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; **$1M** Meta corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund
• **Sam Altman** -- **$0** direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; **$1M** personal donation to Trump inaugural fund
• **Tim Cook / Apple** -- **$0** direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; **$1M** personal donation to Trump inaugural fund (reported alongside other CEOs)
• **Alphabet / Google** -- **$0** direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; **$1M** corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund
• **Murdoch family** -- No consolidated public 2024 presidential campaign figure (influence mainly via media networks; not publicly itemized for Trump vs Harris) -- (inaugural not reported)
• **Sinclair family** -- No consolidated public 2024 presidential campaign figure (influence mainly via media ownership and PAC activity; not publicly itemized for Trump vs Harris) -- (inaugural not reported)
### Third, diverse inputs protect you from getting trapped.
Auditing diverse media sources helps us avoid one-sided narratives or political silos, especially when algorithms are optimizing your feed for what keeps you scrolling, not what makes you informed.
This has a real demographic component.
According to the Pew Research, 87 percent of Americans age 65 and older still consume news through television, while only 47 percent of those ages 18 to 29 do.
That is a 40-point gap.
At the same time, 93 percent of 18 to 29 year olds consume news on digital devices, compared with 71 percent of those 65 and older. That means tens of millions of younger Americans are operating in a primarily digital news environment, while older Americans remain anchored in broadcast.
Then layer on social media: roughly 55 percent of TikTok users say they get news there, about 48 to 49 percent of Rumble users rely on it for news, roughly 50 percent of Truth Social users do the same (right wing), and around 30 percent of Bluesky (left wing) users say it is a news source for them.
Platforms that barely mattered as distribution systems a few years ago now function as primary news pipelines. That changes what people see, how quickly they see it, and what gets filtered out entirely.
It also means that when two people discuss the same issue, they may not just disagree. They may have consumed it through entirely different informational ecosystems.

How does that change how we even communicate about the SAME news?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0611b4e5-49e2-4a16-9397-7021375de408?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.pewresearch.org/journalism/fact-sheet/news-platform-fact-sheet/](https://substack.com/redirect/94e7edaa-6d1c-41bd-b5cb-cadd68dad5e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[https://www.pewresearch.org/journalism/fact-sheet/social-media-and-news-fact-sheet/](https://substack.com/redirect/94e7edaa-6d1c-41bd-b5cb-cadd68dad5e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### Fourth, auditing your media safeguards your mental clarity.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f35a1bf6-7759-4137-8b0b-a0a8c7ad8a06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Sometimes the stress is not coming from "the news."**
It's coming from the volume, the conflict, the emotional manipulation, and the constant urgency. Too many headlines, too many takes, too many contradictions can lead to analysis paralysis, where you stop forming your own view because you are stuck in the churn of other people's views. Or you stay loyal to a source out of habit, even as the tone, ownership, or incentives shift over time.
Auditing is how you catch that before it starts shaping you.
* * *
## **The Practical Audit Checklist**
Here's the checklist I gave people. It forces you to stop consuming passively and start interrogating what you're being fed:
❏ Who is this made for? Demographic targeting: age, race, gender, income, education
❏ Who owns it? Independent vs. corporate vs. political ties
❏ Who funds it? Ads, subscriptions, donors, VC's, sponsors
❏ What are the incentives? Ratings, clicks, outrage, access, influence
❏ Political alignment? Explicit party support or consistent ideological framing
❏ What's emphasized vs. ignored? Headlines, omissions, framing, tone
❏ Original reporting or recycled? First-hand sourcing vs. commentary, or opinion news
❏ Timing matters! Before election, after election, during controversy. Ambulance chasers?
❏ Emotional manipulation check! Fear, anger, tribal language, moral panic
❏ Who benefits if you believe this? Political, financial, institutional gain, ads
* * *
## **My Media Ranking Exercise**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2186e283-7e70-4078-b1d8-bf2c5165760e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
One of the most useful things I did was rank my own media.
I pulled up the political outlets and personalities I read, watch, and listen to. I literally grabbed their thumbnails, dropped them into the program, I linked below, and forced myself to grade them using the checklist. Not based on whether I agree with them, as I listen to plenty of people I do not agree with, but based on trust, incentives, transparency, ownership, consistency, and whether I clearly understand what they get out of me believing what they are saying.
I kept the grading simple and disciplined:
**S Tier:** Fully transparent ownership and incentives, consistent editorial standards, clear separation of news and opinion, prompt visible corrections, and a mission that prioritizes informing over provoking. I know exactly what they are and what they are not.
**A Tier:** Strong long-term track record, mostly transparent incentives, predictable and manageable bias, and generally reliable corrections. Reporting is prioritized over engagement tactics.
**B Tier:** Useful but inconsistent, with solid reporting mixed with engagement-driven framing. Standards vary, and incentives sometimes influence tone or emphasis.
**C Tier:** Frequently inconsistent, emotionally framed, and blurred between reporting and opinion. Engagement incentives often feel louder than facts, and correction culture is weak.
**D Tier:** Opaque incentives, manipulative framing, outrage-first business model, minimal accountability, and low commitment to factual integrity.
The point is **not** to eliminate everything that is not an S. The point is to know where everything sits.
That exercise forces honesty. Some sources moved up. Some moved down. Some surprised me. And the biggest benefit was clarity.
[https://tiermaker.com/](https://substack.com/redirect/54fc3b18-9d14-4fb2-85f4-19d9aaf753c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## **This Is Not About Loyalty**
We are not going back to a world where everybody watches the same evening news and reads the same front page. The ecosystem is expanding, fragmenting, and speeding up. That means the only rational response is literacy: understanding incentives, understanding framing, understanding ownership, and understanding how distribution shapes perception.
Audit your media! The companies already audited you.

The result is not just "more options." The result is that two people can follow politics every day and still have almost no shared starting point. Even when the topic is the same, the framing is different, the omissions are different, and the emotional cues are different. That gap is why conversations feel impossible sometimes. It is not just polarization. It is informational and cultural drift. Why Auditing Your Media Matters This is the core idea I tried to communicate in the presentation. Auditing your media is not about telling people what to watch. It's about teaching yourself how to examine what you are already consuming, and why you are consuming it. First, misinformation is rampant across all platforms. Auditing helps you identify credible sources versus misleading ones. And I'm not saying that as a cheap shot at one side. Misinformation shows up as outright falsehoods, as selective context, as emotionally loaded framing, and as headlines that are technically "true" while still being designed to push you toward a conclusion before you even read the first sentence. Auditing forces you to slow down and ask: is this outlet credible, consistent, and transparent, or is it an engagement machine that happens to report news sometimes? There are practical tools that help with this. Platforms like how the same story is covered across outlets and assign bias ratings using independent evaluators such as AllSides, Ad Fontes Media, and Media Bias Fact Check. Sites like allow you to look up specific publications and review their factual reporting history and ideological lean. And when you are dealing with viral claims, manipulated images, or AI-generated content, fact-checking resources like can provide verification before you share something that simply feels true. The point is not to outsource your thinking. The point is to give yourself instruments to test what you're being told before it quietly becomes part of your worldview. | | ---|---|--- Second, ownership matters. Different platform owners and political contributions influence content. That does not mean every article is propaganda. It means incentives exist. If a platform's business model is ads and engagement, the incentives will lean toward outrage, certainty, and tribal language. If an outlet is owned by a corporate conglomerate or a billionaire with political interests, that does not automatically invalidate everything they publish. It does mean you should understand the ecosystem you're swimming in. And it also means you should be skeptical of the idea that any outlet is "above" bias just because it uses the right vocabulary. | | ---|---|--- 2024 Presidential Campaign Cycle - Major Donors & Inaugural Contributions From Chat GPT • Elon Musk -- ~$291M to pro-Trump/GOP super PACs & campaigns in 2024 cycle; $0 reported to Harris ; (no separate inaugural number needed to show scale) • Jeff Bezos / Amazon (PAC ecosystem) -- ~$11 -17M in federal PAC giving that leaned Republican (not itemized by Trump vs Harris); $1M Amazon corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund • Larry Ellison -- ~$15M to GOP-aligned super PACs in 2024 cycle; no public itemized Harris amount; (inaugural not reported) • Mark Zuckerberg / Meta -- $0 direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; $1M Meta corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund • Sam Altman -- $0 direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; $1M personal donation to Trump inaugural fund • Tim Cook / Apple -- $0 direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; $1M personal donation to Trump inaugural fund (reported alongside other CEOs) • Alphabet / Google -- $0 direct to Trump campaign reported; no clear Harris campaign total reported; $1M corporate donation to Trump inaugural fund • Murdoch family -- No consolidated public 2024 presidential campaign figure (influence mainly via media networks; not publicly itemized for Trump vs Harris) -- (inaugural not reported) • Sinclair family -- No consolidated public 2024 presidential campaign figure (influence mainly via media ownership and PAC activity; not publicly itemized for Trump vs Harris) -- (inaugural not reported) Third, diverse inputs protect you from getting trapped. Auditing diverse media sources helps us avoid one-sided narratives or political silos, especially when algorithms are optimizing your feed for what keeps you scrolling, not what makes you informed. This has a real demographic component. According to the Pew Research, 87 percent of Americans age 65 and older still consume news through television, while only 47 percent of those ages 18 to 29 do. That is a 40-point gap. At the same time, 93 percent of 18 to 29 year olds consume news on digital devices, compared with 71 percent of those 65 and older. That means tens of millions of younger Americans are operating in a primarily digital news environment, while older Americans remain anchored in broadcast. Then layer on social media: roughly 55 percent of TikTok users say they get news there, about 48 to 49 percent of Rumble users rely on it for news, roughly 50 percent of Truth Social users do the same (right wing), and around 30 percent of Bluesky (left wing) users say it is a news source for them. Platforms that barely mattered as distribution systems a few years ago now function as primary news pipelines. That changes what people see, how quickly they see it, and what gets filtered out entirely. It also means that when two people discuss the same issue, they may not just disagree. They may have consumed it through entirely different informational ecosystems. How does that change how we even communicate about the SAME news? | | ---|---|--- Fourth, auditing your media safeguards your mental clarity. | | ---|---|--- Sometimes the stress is not coming from "the news." It's coming from the volume, the conflict, the emotional manipulation, and the constant urgency. Too many headlines, too many takes, too many contradictions can lead to analysis paralysis, where you stop forming your own view because you are stuck in the churn of other people's views. Or you stay loyal to a source out of habit, even as the tone, ownership, or incentives shift over time. Auditing is how you catch that before it starts shaping you. The Practical Audit Checklist Here's the checklist I gave people. It forces you to stop consuming passively and start interrogating what you're being fed: ❏ Who is this made for? Demographic targeting: age, race, gender, income, education ❏ Who owns it? Independent vs. corporate vs. political ties ❏ Who funds it? Ads, subscriptions, donors, VC's, sponsors ❏ What are the incentives? Ratings, clicks, outrage, access, influence ❏ Political alignment? Explicit party support or consistent ideological framing ❏ What's emphasized vs. ignored? Headlines, omissions, framing, tone ❏ Original reporting or recycled? First-hand sourcing vs. commentary, or opinion news ❏ Timing matters! Before election, after election, during controversy. Ambulance chasers? ❏ Emotional manipulation check! Fear, anger, tribal language, moral panic ❏ Who benefits if you believe this? Political, financial, institutional gain, ads My Media Ranking Exercise | | ---|---|--- One of the most useful things I did was rank my own media. I pulled up the political outlets and personalities I read, watch, and listen to. I literally grabbed their thumbnails, dropped them into the program, I linked below, and forced myself to grade them using the checklist. Not based on whether I agree with them, as I listen to plenty of people I do not agree with, but based on trust, incentives, transparency, ownership, consistency, and whether I clearly understand what they get out of me believing what they are saying. I kept the grading simple and disciplined: S Tier: Fully transparent ownership and incentives, consistent editorial standards, clear separation of news and opinion, prompt visible corrections, and a mission that prioritizes informing over provoking. I know exactly what they are and what they are not. A Tier: Strong long-term track record, mostly transparent incentives, predictable and manageable bias, and generally reliable corrections. Reporting is prioritized over engagement tactics. B Tier: Useful but inconsistent, with solid reporting mixed with engagement-driven framing. Standards vary, and incentives sometimes influence tone or emphasis. C Tier: Frequently inconsistent, emotionally framed, and blurred between reporting and opinion. Engagement incentives often feel louder than facts, and correction culture is weak. D Tier: Opaque incentives, manipulative framing, outrage-first business model, minimal accountability, and low commitment to factual integrity. The point is not to eliminate everything that is not an S. The point is to know where everything sits. That exercise forces honesty. Some sources moved up. Some moved down. Some surprised me. And the biggest benefit was clarity. This Is Not About Loyalty We are not going back to a world where everybody watches the same evening news and reads the same front page. The ecosystem is expanding, fragmenting, and speeding up. That means the only rational response is literacy: understanding incentives, understanding framing, understanding ownership, and understanding how distribution shapes perception. Audit your media! The companies already audited you. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by support Matt's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

## Board of Peace Pledges $5B
President Trump announced Sunday that members of his newly created Board of Peace have pledged $5 billion toward [Gaza reconstruction efforts](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO6yAURL8Gd0RwDSYpKF7jLq_d0rrAJWZFwMIkUfbrV84vbD1nZqTzdV2umHIqt_94J9tjXQq99ky9U1tcxRZq3Ag9YU5UdiwB_aMtIGDiAricloApvxc1BBuJgMaBrDRGghIgp2G1jqIKNEUdHSilnUDlwHmKeIlaiMuQ7LF20FJKIfVp1MadYzBnQ1KZIJgSFFKv7fRdU-krxfyuT2onX-9Dtmvv287GfwxmBnNfaU05HxmDeas5-TeDOZVOrWBPtWBmMGszXvRZc81dyjnVwm_4g7yRr2Xv7eEPkn8E8Br5RwGDeWg2bK-jsU-GKXG7Y_p8Df1P8p4WfgMAAP__BlCEUw) and will commit thousands of personnel to maintain security. The pledges will be formally announced at the board's [inaugural meeting on Feb. 19](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SozAQhJ8GMlHS8CMTKLiEzJdeSA3MCOtKSJQkm_U-_RZ-hY37q67--t99vqPzLmx_cWdTbJwDn9lzKZzmJWKiaA_GldE7DhkD4fpMM0gYhAShhpnQ-ffc1WQsM3Bbs1FaK-gkqKF-mI4WbEcJg231OBIuNHIPWt_YUqeAa2eutotWSknVN22vl5slfdOsOk2y6iSTKzE1_6ML5cHWv-OLU7PGvfbmUcqRq_ZPBVMF03mejY1fl8WVVzAd0bvi1lzBVNJzPwSGEJ9h5Sx6sTjvXQzi8Ewbiw2_UaAj8VEXH3Ox875wynUydJwXnwdddXLb0fnPhvKr414GfgIAAP__N5-EFw) at the Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace in Washington. Indonesia became the first firm commitment, with up to 8,000 troops expected to be ready by June for potential deployment as part of a humanitarian mission. More than 20 countries have accepted invitations to join, including Israel, the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, and Saudi Arabia. The UN estimates Gaza's full reconstruction needs at [roughly $70 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ_GdEZe82MoXKShu7Qp0cKuOScGI-M7dHn6iHuF1PNpRt983cYb-uC35RNXttnFcePzCJwzp3GKmCi6nXFmDJ63AzfC-ZFGrXQrlZbQjoQ-vMa6IOuYNVcFWzAGdK00tMXddlVPxGCwxsbNNZBqVdXPs3NIHXRQeHu1XTQAKGjKqjFT58h0hqE2pEStmHyOqfyOfst3duEVn5zKOa5FsPec90NUH0IPQg_neZZ0XpHQA29CDzk91l2-XWR08m0jJ5x_OB1yD0wLy0ZOPgQfN-likgv-otADStP0nYa-KZKl_byIozWiVsuKPrzn878-e1r9FwAA__9kRH9g).
## Olympic Rivals Get Engaged
Former Team USA ice dancer Jean-Luc Baker proposed to Spanish skater Olivia Smart on Valentine's Day in the streets of Milan, exactly four years after confessing his love to her at the 2022 Beijing Olympics. [See photos here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGP3CAQBeBfgztWMGbhrqBIQ3dpU1pjM_ZOgsEC4pX_feT8havf06en9-tr-kJOnLefuJPva5kyvVui3qlOc8Eay3oQLoSJKTfMEZe_dQIFViqQ2k4ROV2TGaJfiYDGgbx2ToNRoO3w8gu62YJ9jqud3aJGbbS2q4n608TlE-3A_tbuttZa6edjfLr5Y43uw5E2LiphFEXupT5-F879RWu6ykn1sZR9SP7V-9HE-ENAEBDydZTW70hAuGEBQYGAoJ8CQjtK7U1AKOnaD15k-4Od8yYrn5ia3KhLyhtuFCVnuXPCLEuWJybKnTM1GfESEIbq4_HmlLhZJ4zaduT0f1D_1ounh38BAAD__6FchXA). Smart and Baker were once rivals who competed against each other at two World Championships and the Beijing Games, where Smart finished eighth, and Baker placed [11th in ice dance](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd1jwTIxTUGzjLttuaT3Dw2YHgwUkUf5-5PmFkW55dK_u-fdYHhhiSNtfPMg0n5dE7xqpNSrLmrG47E9CSxgDpYrJoX2WBQSMXACX4-IwxM-iOmc8EdDQkZFaS1AC5NjtxqIaBNDNenF3gyKl_H21zgKOk1untQvmartoKaWQt3646XXyTk-apNJOMCXIhZZL_z-H1Hby8ZNfVHqbjy6avbWzsuEPg5nBbLGvZy6t9h_cc74YBvN1isFcT0yh7tyH7VmI1y9sVPhGrXJKG27kOAg5XJn6vR2xK8ad7xBjqKNmSmwHhviz234l62XgOwAA___H_35U). Baker won bronze in the team event at the 2018 PyeongChang Olympics with partner Kaitlin Hawayek, but hasn't competed since 2023 due to injuries. Smart, 28, recently finished ninth with partner Tim Dieck at the Milan Games. Baker, 32, carried the engagement ring throughout Smart's competition, [waiting for her events to conclude](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuhDAQheHTQGdkDyxmCxdp6DZtSjTYA0w02Mg4i_b20eYK6T89Pf1fj-mBLBzXT9zJlSVNka5TqBTK05wwh7QchJ5QmOKJMaD_yRNo6JUGZfopIMtr6urgFiKgtiZnrDXQaTB9vTk_EwYDcPdI2vc3O9x1uIMHaoehNX3N7r321sYYbW5Ne7PzsAQ7WDKdDbrqNAUuKTffiWPZaJFXelJufNprcVspx1m1HxWMFYzXdTVlo5lXIQxvUsGYhJ-M6twxF0VxxZWCymnHWNirI6cjnSgKi7o4FsoqyWs_2J-Ko9pZMFYw1tmF42IRPntbdXrdkeXvQ_lXuKeD3wAAAP__MVqEJQ) before popping the question.
## Chart: Political Affiliation by Generation
More than half of Gen Z and Millennials now identify as political independents rather than [Republicans or Democrats](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uhDAQBOCngc7INj_mChdp6C5tSrTg9bHRno3M3qF7--iSR0g50qcZab6u8xWIKd0-4Y5eYp4TngejCJZ5yVBCjjvCisCE6YAUYH2U2Wo7KG2VGeYAxK-5q4OPiBbbGr1xzthOWzPUmx_aLi6DCV0f4DIuK4TLZVi0GR0gxH6pyb_b3toYo03ftL1bxhjc6NB0Luiq0xhIcmm-MyXZMPIrP7E0a77X7DeR_ajaj8pOlZ3O82yedDyAV9hJgOmQN6zstG5QBIPaM5PQCqwgRmICoZzU8lI3TFj-EiUlG6qHOio71cWH_SRmOgZXdfp2B-LfdfnXZU9vfwIAAP__sxCCZg), according to new Gallup data. Among Gen Z, 56% identify as independent compared to just 17% Republican and 27% Democrat, while 54% of Millennials also [reject party labels](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFutDAQhJ_GdCDbGMwVLv6G7v42JVrsBTbasy3w3YW3j0geIfX3aWY0H_fpDsQU1__wQFeWNEV8H4yl4D7NCfaQlozgEZgwHhAD-Oc-aan7Wupa9VMA4nMyVXALosa2QqesVdpIrfpqc15ppWYYfO_n-WY6MH6Q2re99B22bajIXWmXrZSSqmvazs7DEuxgURkbpDASA5W0N5-JYtlw4TO9cG98elTstlLyIdp_Qo9Cj9f8ZgXmZ7640GNOzEKPVkpzu_0a9UbrVlPAWGg565yYCnngmmLAjPECRwNH_qp2F_KbmOnorTByfQDxT3H501svp78DAAD__51Ofqo). This marks a dramatic shift from previous generations—in 1992, only 40% of Gen X identified as independent at the same age. The trend reverses among older Americans. The Silent Generation [remains the most partisan](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL_u4yAQhJ8Gd0SA_-AUFNe4y7VXWmtY4j2twQKSKG9_8r3Cr_4-jWbmz2N9ADGl52840LWY14SfytgalnXLUEKOJ4JHYMJUIQXwr7IaZSapjNTTGoD4uw5dcBHRYN-h09ZqMyijp253_r7ZqLZ-DBijxdmbbQsj9HBXc4-D7chdaZettVZ6vPWj3eYY7GxRDzYoMSgM1HK5_c2U2o6Rv_mN5ebz0bHbWzur6H8JswizwObtNeGCwixnrk2Y5QnMr1OemVnWPX-qPHJBCQcW8pCqhIKSAqZG8Xtp1MgDS0oBT0wXqMIseu7verKzMEtXXDg_xEx1smJQzwOI_zdqP7rx7cy_AAAA__-KQ4gL), with roughly seven in 10 identifying with either major party after coming of age during the post-WWII era and early Cold War. Overall, 45% of all U.S. adults now identify as independents, up from one-third two decades ago.
